sections.name: File setup, Sub, SUBS, Illustrative, YardTag, pct, recordedText, months, ListSpec
sections.title: Imports, tag labels and display helpers
sections.what: Brings in libraries, shared components and types. Defines the Illustrative and Yard tags, formatting for percentages and months, a helper that turns capital-letter codes into readable words, and the four sub-view names.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the marks that separate placeholders from recorded facts the same across the page.
sections.watch_out: The Illustrative tag warns that numbers are placeholders, so removing it would make placeholder backlog look sourced.

sections.name: BuildAdvisor
sections.title: Page frame with four tabs
sections.what: Loads the advisor data, shows a loading state and an error message with a retry button, and displays an intro with contractor and project counts. Switches between the four views and opens the project popup and citation drawer.
sections.why: Likely reason: one entry point loads the data once and passes it to every tab.
sections.watch_out: Data is cached for five minutes, so a newly recorded project may not appear until the cache expires or the page reloads.

sections.name: ProjectList
sections.title: Project list with sources
sections.what: Lists projects in a popup with their industry, country and stage, the contractor as recorded, the delivery model with its recorded wording, and the cost and delay outcome. Source buttons open the citation. Long delivery wording is cut to about 160 characters.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the owner check each claim against its source.
sections.watch_out: Cutting long text happens before the wording is cleaned up, so the cut can fall mid-word.

sections.name: PlanBuild
sections.title: Plan a build: fit, structure and partners
sections.what: Lets the owner choose industry, region, size, owner capability, top priority and technology. Ranks delivery models with the best fit first, and the owner can pick another. Shows structure guidance, a button to see Yard precedents, and a partner table ranked by recorded projects then by illustrative headroom.
sections.why: Likely reason: turns the owner's choices into a ranked starting point.
sections.watch_out: The ranking leans partly on placeholder scores, so the top model is only as firm as those placeholders.

sections.name: ProfileBars
sections.title: Illustrative profile dots
sections.what: Shows five ratings for the chosen delivery model: cost and schedule certainty, speed, owner effort, flexibility to change, and suitability for novel technology. Each is drawn as five dots.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the Illustrative label.
sections.watch_out: These ratings are placeholder profiles, not measured outcomes.

sections.name: HeatTable
sections.title: Shared count grid for this page
sections.what: Builds a count table from rows and columns supplied by the caller. Filled cells are shaded by size relative to the largest cell and clicking reports the row and column. Empty cells show a dot labelled None recorded. Each row has a total.
sections.why: Likely reason: a lighter version of the Analysis grid, kept separate for this page.
sections.watch_out: Only row totals are shown, unlike the Analysis grid which also shows column totals.

sections.name: EpcMap
sections.title: Contractor map by region and market depth
sections.what: Has two modes. Contractors × region ranks up to 24 contractors by recorded projects, filtered by industry and region, with a click for their profile or a cell for their projects. Market depth counts distinct contractors recorded for each industry and region. Region buttons filter the grid.
sections.why: Likely reason: owners see where competition is, and EPCs see where few rivals have a record.
sections.watch_out: Only the top 24 contractors appear, and contractor names are counted as recorded, so spelling variants may appear as separate firms.

sections.name: DeliveryModels
sections.title: Delivery model experience and outcomes
sections.what: Shows a grid of delivery models by industry, then a table with project counts, median cost against plan, median delay and a short profile for each model. Clicking a model opens its projects.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives owners precedents and outcomes for each delivery model.
sections.watch_out: Medians come from small samples, and the page asks readers to treat them as precedent, not a benchmark.

sections.name: Contractors
sections.title: Contractor search and profile
sections.what: A searchable list of up to 120 contractors, filterable by industry. The selected contractor's profile shows recorded projects, work in delivery now, recorded median cost and delay, placeholder backlog and headroom, and chips that open projects by industry, region and delivery model. Part of the chip line is cut off in the packet.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets an owner check one contractor's record in one place.
sections.watch_out: When nothing is selected, the first matching contractor is shown, so the profile changes as the search narrows without a click.

summary: The owner and contractor planning page. It recommends a delivery model for one capital build, shows structure guidance, and lists partners and Yard precedents.
purpose: Helps an owner or an EPC (a firm that engineers, procures and builds a project) plan one build using what the Yard records about delivery models, contractors and outcomes.
why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the intro text. The page labels recorded facts and placeholder numbers separately so users do not mistake one for the other.
how: 1. Loads advisor data once and keeps it for five minutes. 2. Shows one of four tabs: plan a build, EPC map, delivery models, or contractor profiles. 3. In plan mode, the owner chooses settings and the page ranks delivery models. 4. It shows structure guidance and a shortlist of contractors. 5. Clicking a name or count opens a project list with sources.
inputs: Advisor data from getBuildAdvisor (projects, contractors, industries, regions, delivery labels and delivery sources), the owner's plan choices, and clicks.
outputs: Four views, a ranked list of delivery models, a partner table, project popups, and source citations.
risks: Backlog, headroom and profile scores are placeholders, and the top recommendation depends on them. Medians come from small samples. Contractor names may not match across records. Changing a plan choice clears any manual model pick.
debug: If the page will not load, check the data request in getBuildAdvisor and use the retry button. If a tab is empty, check whether the data holds projects for that industry or region. If rankings look wrong, check recommend and shortlist in the advisor module, which this file imports but does not show.
